messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-generation.p99 latency breach detected for prod-us-west. p99 = 18.4s (SLO 5s). Error rate for streaming chains + auth failures spiked. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): seeing it in console — tail latency climbing since 03:12 UTC. Rolling traces now.

ankit (sre): I have the traces open. Lots of backend waits on config-fetch and token-store calls from inference-sidecars. DB auth read latencies ~600ms.

julia (eng-runtime): confirmed: controlplane config service is returning 503s intermittently; sidecars are blocking while fetching per-req feature flags. Streaming requests are waiting for initial config handshake.

maria (oncall): customer impact? any errors surfaced to clients?

kevin (support): Support dashboards show increased timeouts for a small subset of heavy streaming customers, ~4% of calls failing with 504. A couple of customers opened realtime complaints.

ankit (sre): quick numbers: p95 ~2.3s, p99 ~18.4s, streaming stall count up +280% since spike. Error rate for /v1/streaming generate up from 0.3% to 4.9%.

incident-bot: @maria @ankit @julia oncall-escalation: page severity P1 — assign if help needed.

maria (oncall): I'm taking it. Handoff note added. Priorities: (1) restore SLO for streaming reads, (2) minimize customer errors, (3) identify root cause for controlplane slowness.

ankit (sre): first mitigation: enable local config cache on sidecars to bypass repeated controlplane calls. Patch is in staging. Will push a quick rollout to prod with traffic weighting. Command: 
```
kubectl -n prod rollout restart ds/inference-sidecar && kubectl set env ds/inference-sidecar SIDE_CACHED_CONFIG=enabled --record
```

julia (eng-runtime): preparing a canary: 5% traffic to sidecars with cached config. Also reducing config-fetch TTL to 300s only for canary so we can revert quickly.

maria (oncall): ankit, can you also check DB read replica pool? If token-store reads are hot, we might need to scale read-replicas or enable local token cache fallback.

ankit (sre): scaling replica group now: `sqlctl replicas add --cluster=auth-tokens --count=2` - should add capacity in ~90s. Meanwhile enabling short-lived local token cache on sidecars (80ms TTL). Rolling that change now.

sre-bot: Replica scaling job started (job id r-33f2). Estimated completion 72s.

kevin (support): Posting interim customer note: "We are investigating increased latency for streaming responses; some requests may timeout. Engineers are applying mitigations now." Will send to affected customers once we see improvement.

(2m later)

ankit (sre): DB replicas are up. Observability: token-store p99 dropped from 620ms -> 120ms after local cache and replica scale.

julia (eng-runtime): canary rollout shows p99 streaming dropped to 5.8s for canary traffic. Rolling cached-config to 40% then 100% if stable.

maria (oncall): go for 40% then full. Keep monitoring.

(5m later)

incident-bot: metric alert cleared for controlplane error-rate (now 0.7%). However p99 streaming still at 6.1s, slightly above target.

ankit (sre): remaining tail spikes appear correlated with large model KV cache warmups + some requests still hitting config-fetch for feature-flag checks. I'm going to temporarily turn off synchronous feature-flag fetch on hot path: set `FEATUREFLAG_SYNC=false` in sidecars.

julia (eng-runtime): applying that flag now to 100% — it's a safe short-circuit: if cache miss, assume default false for non-critical flags.

maria (oncall): after that change p99 dropped to 3.7s; p95 1.9s. Error rate back to baseline 0.35%. Streaming stalls reduced.

kevin (support): notifying customers now — sending polite update, offering credits for impacted minutes.

carter (pm): any customer-visible data we should include? rough timeline + % of calls affected + mitigation steps?

kevin (support): sending: start 03:12 UTC, mitigations (local config cache, token replica scale, feature-flag short-circuit) rolled 03:16-03:24 UTC. Estimated affected calls ~4% of streaming calls for ~12 minutes.

maria (oncall): current status: degraded -> recovered, continuing to monitor for 30m. Opening incident ticket for postmortem. Assigning owner: julia.

julia (eng-runtime): I’ll own the postmortem. Initial hypothesis: sudden spike in controlplane CPU/DB contention caused config service 503s; sidecars blocked synchronously leading to head-of-line stalls for streaming. Root causes to validate: (1) config-fetch fanout pattern on cold-sidecars, (2) token-store read hotkeys, (3) feature flag fetch path blocking path.

ankit (sre): runbook changes during incident: suggest adding defensive defaults (non-blocking flag fetch), extend local config TTL, introduce circuit-breaker around config service, and autoscale controlplane earlier on CPU spike.

maria (oncall): post-incident action items (triage):
- julia: postmortem draft (include timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation steps)
- ankit: add token-store read autoscaling and cache metrics (ETA 48h)
- infra: add controlplane CPU autoscale policy and circuit-breaker (ETA 72h)
- docs: update runbook to prefer local config cache for streaming (ETA 24h)

julia (eng-runtime): noted. Starting postmortem doc now and will tag owners.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by maria (oncall) — severity degraded to SEV-RECOVERED at 03:28 UTC.

maria (oncall): marking handoff to next oncall in 20m. Thanks all. Will update #incidents with postmortem link once julia publishes. :thumbsup:

kevin (support): closing customer-notification thread after confirmations.

sre-bot: Reminder scheduled: postmortem review meeting in 48h (invites pending).

julia (eng-runtime): adding initial notes to postmortem: logs show surge of controlplane requests originating from ~200 new sidecar pods in a short window; investigate rollout/scale event correlation.

maria (oncall): final status: resolved. Root cause work assigned. If anything regresses ping me directly.

(End of thread)
